findings.defect: The draft assigns the fulfilled promise to Jeok Cheongang rather than to the Disciple who has returned.
findings.rationale: Taekyung speaks after enduring the transformation to return. The Korean leaves the subject implicit; the scene supports Taekyung reporting that he kept his promise.

findings.current: They thought only of the Master’s grief-stricken hands clutching his Disciple’s body as he sobbed, or the battle’s echoes that still hadn’t faded. Or perhaps they thought it was simply their imagination.
findings.defect: The witnesses are attributing the finger’s movement to other causes, not merely thinking about the Master’s hands or the battlefield.
findings.rationale: The Korean lists the explanations the witnesses gave for what they saw, establishing why they missed the sign of life.
findings.replacement: They put the movement down to the grieving Master’s hands as he held his Disciple’s body and sobbed, the lingering vibrations of the battlefield—or simply their imagination.
findings.source: 그저 제자의 시신을 끌어안고 오열하는 스승의 비통한 손길이나 아직도 멎지 않은 전장의 울림. 혹은 단순한 착각이라고 생각했을 뿐이었다.

findings.current: They failed to look closely at the quality hidden behind those two words: purification.
findings.defect: “Those two words” carries over a reference to the Korean written term that does not work for the single English word “destruction.”
findings.rationale: The contrast is between fire’s destructive and purifying qualities; the Korean character count need not survive in English.
findings.replacement: They failed to look past destruction and see fire’s power to purify.
findings.source: 소멸이라는 두 글자에 가려진, 정화(淨化)의 성질은 유심히 들여다보지 못한 채.

summary: The closing line reverses who kept the promise; an earlier passage also obscures why the witnesses dismissed the moving finger.
